bindings_basis.text: The dataset file the id came from: lakes_directory (lake), the RFR reaches in geo/freshwater_waters.geojson (river), spear_entry_points (spear), the CO-OPS and NDBC station tables in tide_stations.json (coast), the hunt_deer.json zone records (deerzone), the hunt codes drawn in geo/archery_hunts.geojson and geo/additional_hunts.geojson (hunt), geo/waterfowl_zones.geojson (wfzone), the Type A wildlife areas the public-land layer classifies under 14 CCR section 551(e) (wfarea), the CDFW ecological reserves, wildlife areas, public access properties and fish hatcheries drawn in geo/public_lands.geojson (publicland), and the named BLM wilderness and wilderness study units drawn in geo/blm_wilderness.geojson (wilderness), the named national forests drawn in geo/usfs_forest_ownership.geojson (forest) and the named Forest Service wilderness units drawn in geo/usfs_wilderness.geojson (usfswilderness). The last two are keyed on the NAME the Forest Service layer publishes rather than on its feature id: the ownership layer publishes two ids for Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, and the wilderness layer's ids are the small integers the CDFW public-land layer already publishes for its own properties, so either choice would publish one place twice or bind two places to one id. The kind and the id together are the reference: a publicland row's id is the public-land feature's own id, so the property's own hunting sentence, its citation, its restrictions and CDFW's own access sentence are read from the record the row is keyed on; a wilderness row's id is the NLCS feature's own id, so the unit's designation and that layer's own designation wording are read from the record the row is keyed on. This file carries the reference and never the prose.

A bitset of the activities this app records for the place's own file: freshwater for a lake or a reach, saltwater and spearfishing for a coastal access point, big game for a deer zone and for an area-specific deer hunt, waterfowl for a waterfowl zone, and waterfowl with upland for a Type A wildlife area, whose own classification names both kinds of bird season. A CDFW public-land property carries big game, upland and waterfowl together where the lands booklet publishes a hunting sentence for that property, and no activity bit at all where the booklet publishes none, in which case the property's own record carries the sentence saying so. A named BLM wilderness or wilderness study unit carries the same three, with that layer's own designation wording as the reference. A national forest and a Forest Service wilderness carry no activity bit, read through the same expression and for the same reason a CDFW property with no published sentence carries none: neither Forest Service layer publishes a hunting block at all. The row exists anyway, so the place can be listed, named and measured against a reader's own point, and what this app knows about the ground is the statute and the caveats that layer already publishes. The three travel together because what puts them on the row is the existence of the published sentence, and which species a sentence covers is a question about the sentence — one this index does not read and does not answer. A NOAA station row carries no activity bit at all — it is a join target, not a published public access point. A bit says this app records the activity for the place. It says nothing about whether a season is open there, which is a question only the dated rule and SeasonCalculator answer.
The nearest CO-OPS station in tide_stations.json by great-circle distance, capped at 40 km, for a coastal place only; null beyond the cap and null for an inland place.
The nearest NDBC station in tide_stations.json's buoy table by great-circle distance, capped at 60 km, for a coastal place only; null beyond the cap and null for an inland place.

The nearest CO-OPS currents-prediction station, capped at 25 km. GAP: this dataset carries no catalog of California currents-prediction stations, so every row is null rather than guessed. It becomes a binding when the catalog is fetched, and not before.

HAND-CURATED. A gage is bound only where the gage and the water share a name, or the gage sits on the named reach; there is no automatic join that is safe here. Null until the curated bindings file names the pair.

The deer or waterfowl zone key, and it is the key the zone's own polygon is published under: a deer-zone row carries its hunt_deer record's geometry_ref, which is a geo/deer_zones id character for character and is the same string the hunt-opportunity rows are matched on; a waterfowl-zone row carries its own geo/waterfowl_zones id. An area-specific hunt carries no zone key — the layers publish a hunt code and a boundary, and reading a zone out of a hunt's title would be this app parsing prose for a join. A CDFW public-land property and a named BLM wilderness unit carry the deer zone whose published polygon in geo/deer_zones CONTAINS that place's own published point, computed in this build by point-in-polygon over that layer, and null where no published zone contains it. Containment, never the nearest zone: a property bound to the zone it is merely closest to would carry a dated season belonging to ground it is not on.

The verbatim AREA NAME string, matched EXACTLY or through a pair of spellings declared in curated/hunt_code_aliases_2026.json, and never fuzzy-matched. This release can match one document: the Type A reservation table in hunt_opportunities.json, whose printed area name is bound where the public-land layer publishes that same name character for character, or where CDFW's two spellings of one place — Gray Lodge WA on the form, Gray Lodge Wildlife Area on the layer — are declared as a pair by the owner, with both documents that carry them. The only difference a declared pair may span is the words Wildlife Area, their abbreviation WA, or their absence, so a row naming a UNIT inside an area still carries no area name rather than its area's. The waterfowl hunt-results document this column also joins to is a live payload this release does not ship, so no row is bound to it.
1 where a satellite sea-surface-temperature pixel is meaningful — a coastal place — and 0 on every other kind of row, hunting rows included.
The composite zoneType:zoneId id of the NWS forecast zone whose published polygon contains the place's own published point, read from geo/nws_zones.geojson. Null where no published zone contains it.

R39. The waterfowl zone whose published polygon in geo/waterfowl_zones contains the place's own published point, computed in this build by point-in-polygon over that layer. Containment, never the nearest zone: a place bound to the zone it is merely closest to would carry a dated season belonging to ground it is not on. It is carried under the spelling the season records are keyed on, which for three of the five zones is the boundary layer's own spelling character for character and for the other two is a pair of spellings declared in curated/hunt_code_aliases_2026.json with both documents that print them: the layer draws Northeastern California Zone and Balance of State, and the waterfowl season document keys the same two zones Northeastern Zone and Balance of State Zone. Those two pairs are recorded in that file as a draft awaiting the owner, who has ruled on the deer-zone codes and on the wildlife-area names and not yet on a waterfowl zone; the file says so in its own words and the build report prints the status beside the count. Nothing else is folded, and a zone that resolves to neither keeps the layer's own spelling rather than a guess. The column is computed for the kinds that are a piece of ground a reader travels to — a lake, a reach, a CDFW public-land property, a named BLM wilderness unit, a national forest and a Forest Service wilderness — and is null on every other kind, because a waterfowl-zone row IS the zone and a NOAA station is not ground. Null where no published zone contains the point. A zone name says which zone the place is in. It says nothing about whether a season is open there, which is a question only the dated rule and SeasonCalculator answer.

R39. Every area-specific hunt code whose published boundary in geo/archery_hunts or geo/additional_hunts contains the place's own published point, separated by a single space, in code order. A LIST and not one code, because those boundaries overlap: of the 295 public-land points this dataset publishes, 87 sit inside one drawn hunt, 23 inside two, 30 inside three and one inside four, so naming a single hunt for a place inside three of them would discard two dated seasons that reach the ground the reader is standing on. A hunt code is one token and no code this dataset draws carries a space or a comma; the build refuses one that does rather than assuming it. Containment, never the nearest hunt, and computed for the same kinds the waterfowl-zone column is computed for. Null where no drawn boundary contains the point, which is the honest answer and not zero: this app draws boundaries for 72 hunt codes and CDFW publishes more hunts than that. A code says which drawn hunt the place is inside. It says nothing about a season, a tag, a quota or a draw.

R40. Every upland game zone whose published boundary in geo/upland_zones contains the place's own published point, separated by a single space, in id order. A LIST and not one zone, because CDFW's quail, band-tailed pigeon and grouse zones are three different species' divisions of the same state and overlap almost everywhere, and because the Mojave National Preserve junior quail area is drawn entirely inside quail Zone Q3 — so a single id would discard two species' zones on nearly every row and would hide the junior season inside the general one. A zone id is one token and no id this layer draws carries a space or a comma; the build refuses one that does rather than assuming it. The id is the LAYER's own key (Quail1, PigeonNorth, GrouseGeneral) and not the season table's row text, because several printed rows share one polygon — CDFW prints three grouse METHOD rows over one grouse zone, and two Zone Q1 rows over one Q1 polygon — so carrying the table's spelling would mean choosing one of them; the pairs that bind a row to a polygon are declared in curated/hunt_code_aliases_2026.json with both documents that carry them. Containment, never the nearest zone, and computed for the same kinds the other two membership columns are computed for. Null where no drawn boundary contains the point. NO SEASON, BAG OR POSSESSION VALUE COMES FROM THAT LAYER: its own season fields were out of date when it was read, and every date this app shows for these species comes from CDFW's Upland Game Birds regulation page. A zone id says which drawn zone the place is inside. It says nothing about whether a season is open there. R41 added an EIGHTH id to that layer and therefore to this column: CrowOpen, CDFW's own polygon of the area American crow hunting is OPEN in, which 1,842 of the 4,575 rows are inside. Its kind is crow_open_area rather than upland_zone, because crow is not an upland game bird — CDFW's own Hunt field on the feature reads Non-game — and because the feature is not a division of the state among zones but the single area the regulation leaves open, with everything outside it closed. It belongs in this column because the column answers exactly one question, which drawn polygon of that file contains this point, and that question is the same for all eight.

Null on every row, and the binding it was reserved for is now made in the other direction. An operator states its own home port; that port is matched to the tide station whose published name carries it; and the operator record in operators.json lists the coastal places within 25 kilometres of that station. So the operator record names its places, this file names no port, and no place here is bound to a port by a name this app matched for it.
